messages:
emma-cs: FYI customer reported an exposed API key in a GitHub gist. They pasted the key here and we saw unusual usage from two IPs. ticket INC-2026 opened.
emma-cs: quick context: customer rotated the key from console at 09:12 UTC but wants us to: 1) confirm old key fully revoked, 2) surface audit logs for the last 7 days, 3) advise on secrets storage + rotation ops.
tom-support: on it. can you paste the console key id and sample of the suspicious calls? even just headers.
emma-cs: key id: key_live_5nB2x. sample logs:
```
2026-02-26T08:47:12Z key=key_live_5nB2x method=/v1/generate ip=13.52.44.1 status=200 tokens=234 prompt_len=60
2026-02-26T09:03:07Z key=key_live_5nB2x method=/v1/embeddings ip=52.66.11.9 status=200 tokens=120 prompt_len=30
```
emma-cs: customer says they rotated at 09:12 but still seeing calls until 09:18 in the snapshot they took.
maria-security: priority: HIGH. We need: (A) immediate confirmation old key is disabled, (B) collection of audit trail (API + console) for 30d for evidence, (C) IOCs (IPs, user agents), (D) guidance to customer on short-term mitigations.
maria-security: Tom — please run the revoke + rotation verification script in the playbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/secrets-incident
ops-oncall: infra-bot will emit a revoke event if you call the key-management API. Use `POST /internal/v1/keys/revoke` with `key_id` and include `x-internal-auth` header.

tom-support: doing step 1 now. curl I ran (internal):
```
curl -X POST https://internal-api.redwood.company/internal/v1/keys/revoke \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SERVICE_TOKEN" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"key_id":"key_live_5nB2x","reason":"suspected leak via GH gist"}'
```

infra-bot: [automated] revoke received for key_live_5nB2x by tom-support at 2026-02-26T09:25:06Z. status=revoked.

tom-support: confirm: revoked at 09:25 UTC. running queries to verify no traffic accepted post-revoke.
dave-sre: I queried the edge logs — last accepted request with that id shows 09:18:45Z, nothing afterwards. Looks like the customer rotation at 09:12 succeeded to create new key but caching + client retries explain the 09:18 calls. I can attach an edge-log slice.

emma-cs: please attach the edge slice and the console audit events so the customer can have them for compliance.
maria-security: for the compliance ask: we keep console audit logs 90 days by default; enterprise customers can enable 365d via retention add-on. For KMS/HSM: explain we use envelope encryption with customer-managed keys (CMK) in KMS for Private deployments and HSM-backed wrapping for on-prem HSM customers. Recommend they enable customer-managed KMS and rotate master keys quarterly.
maria-security: suggested customer message (short): "We revoked the compromised key (key_live_5nB2x) at 09:25 UTC and confirmed no accepted traffic after 09:18 UTC. Please rotate any credentials where that key was embedded. We recommend storing new keys in a secrets manager (HashiCorp Vault, AWS Secrets Manager) and enabling short-lived credentials where possible." :white_check_mark:

tom-support: attaching logs now. edge slice link (internal): https://redwood.logs/edge-slices/2026-02-26/key_live_5nB2x
console audit events:
```
2026-02-26T09:11:59Z user=customer_admin action=create_key id=key_live_X7kP
2026-02-26T09:12:05Z user=customer_admin action=disable_key id=key_live_5nB2x
2026-02-26T09:25:06Z user=tom-support action=revoked_key id=key_live_5nB2x
```

maria-security: add guidance we gave the customer on storage/rotation best practices:
- Don't commit keys to VCS. Use pre-commit hooks to block secrets.
- Use short-lived tokens and session-based creds when possible.
- Store secrets in a secrets manager; use KMS envelope encryption for at-rest secrets.
- Enforce least-privilege policies on keys (scoped to routes/features), and IP allowlisting for high-risk endpoints.
- Set up alerting: token anomaly detection (spike per-key or unknown IPs).

maria-security: sample policy snippets:
```
# HashiCorp Vault KV example (recommended):
path "secret/data/redwood/*" {
  capabilities = ["read"]
}

# AWS Secrets Manager rotation lambda example: store new key under /redwood/api
```

dave-sre: also recommend customer enable per-route rate limits and a short TTL for keys for CI/CD usage. If they embed keys in client-side code, they should move to a backend proxy that mints short-lived tokens.

emma-cs: customer asked about KMS vs HSM — can we provide a short pros/cons line?
maria-security: sure — KMS (cloud): easy, integrated, good for most customers; CMK gives key ownership with API controls. HSM (on-prem/FIPS): higher assurance, hardware root of trust, required for some regulated workloads. HSM adds complexity and will need separate key life-cycle ops and attestation.

tom-support: next action items I recorded on INC-2026:
- [x] revoke compromised key (tom-support)
- [x] verify traffic stopped after revoke (dave-sre)
- [x] provide console audit + edge logs (tom-support)
- [ ] send rotation + storage playbook to customer (emma-cs)
- [ ] recommend KMS/HSM options + retention pricing (maria-security)

maria-security: add: recommend rotation cadence: short-lived API keys for CI (<=24h), service keys rotate monthly, master keys rotate quarterly. For confirmed leaks, immediate rotation + revoke and a full audit.

emma-cs: I'll draft the message and include the snippets + playbook link. tagging @maria-security for the KMS/HSM appendix.

tom-support: one more quick tip for customers: enable RBAC for API key creation in console and require 2FA for key-managing users.

emma-cs: customer update sent. closing loop once they confirm no further alerts. thanks everyone. :pray:
